question.text: A Stakeholder Management Committee within a Cat II AIF is constituted to:

answer.text: Determine the management fee payable to the manager each quarter
Set clear measurable objectives for the fund, design a process to assess investment decisions, and understand the roles/responsibilities/objectives of each stakeholder group
Replace the Investment Committee on material deals
Directly negotiate all definitive agreements on behalf of investee companies

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7.7 (Managing the stakeholders in PE deals), a Stakeholder Management Committee's responsibility is to (i) set clear and measurable objectives for the fund, (ii) design a process to assess investment decisions, and (iii) understand the roles, responsibilities and objectives of each stakeholder group. The Trap: Fee determination is an AMC-level decision. It does NOT replace the IC. It does not negotiate investee agreements. Cross-Exam Context: Stakeholder-management governance tested in XIX-C specifically (less covered in XIX-A). Manager's Pro-Tip: For funds with diverse LPs (SWFs, family offices, pensions), a standing Stakeholder Committee reduces one-off calls from LPs. Publish the Committee's minutes as a summary-digest to preempt individual inquiries.
